verdict.rationale: ByteAsk is documented as a terminal coding agent. It opens a full-screen TUI, reads and edits your codebase, compiles, runs tests and presents a diff, and it also offers a headless `exec` subcommand for scripted runs. Probes of the site and docs llms.txt files confirm the same terminal-native positioning. Missing for 10: independent hands-on corroboration of installing and running the agent locally.

support.subject: As a developer, I can run a coding agent locally from my terminal

citations.quote: ByteAsk opens a full-screen TUI, reads your codebase, edits files, compiles, runs tests, and presents a diff for your review before making permanent changes
It edits your repository from the terminal, then drives the real toolchain
`byteask exec` - it runs one task to completion and exits.
an AI coding agent for C and C++ that runs in your terminal and verifies its own work against the real toolchain
